transcript.content: Hello. What brings you into the clinic today?

Hello, doctor. When I try to talk things through with people, my thoughts get all jumbled and I can’t seem to keep a straight line in a conversation anymore. It has really started to worry me because I just want to be able to speak clearly like I used to.

Along with these difficulties in organizing your thoughts, have you noticed any significant changes in your mood, such as feeling consistently sad, down, or losing interest in things you usually enjoy?

I'm not really sure about those kinds of changes, though of course I still miss my husband very much. I haven't really lost interest in things, it's just that my main struggle is feeling so jumbled and confused when I try to talk or do my activities.
Sometimes when people's thoughts feel jumbled, they might also experience unusual things, like hearing voices or seeing things that others don't. Have you noticed anything like that?

No, I haven't experienced anything like that, doctor. I don't hear any strange voices or see things that aren't there. My trouble is really just with my own thoughts getting all tangled up and confused.
Are you still able to manage your daily activities, like cooking, managing finances, or taking medications, on your own, or do you find you need help with them now?

It has become very difficult for me to manage on my own now. I used to handle my bills and help organize church dinners, but now my daughter has to come over every week to sort my mail and keep track of my appointments. I feel quite embarrassed because the church ladies have even started leaving me off the planning lists because I can't keep up.
How long have you been experiencing these difficulties with your thoughts and activities, and did they start gradually or quite suddenly?

It started gradually, creeping in during the year after my husband passed away, so it has been almost a year now. The really confusing spells where my thoughts and actions feel out of step with everyone have been happening regularly for at least the last six months.
Besides having trouble organizing your thoughts, have you or your daughter noticed any changes in your memory, like forgetting recent conversations or misplacing things more often?

No, I haven't really noticed forgetting recent conversations or misplacing my things. The main issue is just that my thoughts get so jumbled and mixed up when I'm trying to speak to someone or do my daily tasks.
Do you have a history of high blood pressure, heart disease, or have you ever experienced a stroke or sudden weakness on one side of your body?
No, doctor, as far as I know, I don't have any history of high blood pressure or heart disease. I've never had a stroke or experienced any sudden weakness on one side of my body either.
Have you or your daughter noticed any physical changes, such as tremors in your hands, stiffness in your body, or any trouble with your balance when walking?
No, doctor, I haven't noticed any tremors in my hands or stiffness in my body. My balance is also fine, and I don't have any trouble when I'm walking around.
Have your family members, like your daughter, noticed any changes in your personality or behavior, such as acting impulsively, showing less empathy, or saying things that seem out of character?

My daughter has definitely noticed some major changes and was worried enough to bring me to the clinic, though it's not about me being impulsive or lacking empathy. Instead, she has noticed how extremely jumbled I get during conversations, how I struggle to manage my bills, and how I sometimes do odd things like freeze in place or hum to myself.
Have you ever been diagnosed with any other chronic medical or neurological conditions, such as Parkinson's disease, thyroid issues, or kidney disease?

No, doctor, I am not aware of having any chronic medical or neurological conditions like Parkinson's, thyroid issues, or kidney disease. Other than these recent struggles with my jumbled thoughts, my health has generally been okay.
Have you or your family noticed you acting out your dreams while asleep, such as shouting, thrashing around, or kicking?
No, doctor, neither my daughter nor I have noticed anything like that. As far as we know, I don't shout, thrash around, or act out my dreams while I'm asleep.
Even though you feel your memory is fine, has your daughter noticed you repeating the same questions or forgetting recent events?

No, I don't think I repeat questions or forget recent events like that. My daughter is much more concerned about my thoughts getting all mixed up and disorganized, rather than it being a matter of simple forgetfulness.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient presents with progressive cognitive decline characterized by significant difficulties in organizing thoughts, jumbled speech, and executive dysfunction, leading to a loss of independence in activities of daily living (such as managing finances, sorting mail, and planning activities). These symptoms have been present for approximately one year, with persistent impairment for at least six months. While she meets the functional and cognitive decline criteria for dementia, she and her daughter deny prominent memory impairment (forgetfulness, misplacing things, repeating questions), which makes a classic presentation of Alzheimer's disease (F00) less likely. Therefore, Unspecified Dementia (F03) is the most appropriate diagnosis.
